referents.why: 'May it be' (optative) is impersonal; no person is its subject.
'It has been written' is an impersonal passive with no named writer; the builder's 'man' is not the subject of writing.
Second singular inside the quoted words (Psalm 51:4 as quoted): the one spoken to is God, the only second-person candidate, w5.
referents.category: you inside quotation addressed to God

referents.why: Same quoted 'you' in 'will prevail when judged': God.
referents.category: you inside quotation addressed to God

referents.why: 'Your words' (second singular possessive) are God's words, and the addressee of the quotation is God, w5.
'You' as object of 'being judged' (second singular): the one judged is God, w5.

links.why: The hopos clause is the wording of the quotation, not the purpose of the writing; the saying clause introduces it as content.
'It has been written' introduces the quotation, which is what the writing says (ruling R1).
The second quoted clause is part of the quotation, not a purpose of the writing.
Fronted ki is a Hebrew-only category; en tō + infinitive is a temporal adjunct, 'when you are judged'.
links.category: wrong link type for Greek adjunct

links.why: The infinitive phrase 'in being judged' is an adjunct nested inside the clause that governs it.
De after 'may it not be' is adversative: 'let God be true' is said instead of the rejected claim.
links.category: adversative de read as plain and

links.why: De joins two parallel imperatives: 'let God be true, and every man a liar'.
Two verbs of one quoted sentence joined by kai: 'be justified and prevail'.
Kathaper ('just as it is written') is a comparison with a text, not a plain and.
Kathaper ('just as') before a written text: the claim is backed by scripture. The fulfilment sense of 'as' does not apply; see none_fit.

groups.why: The two imperatives at one level, 'let God be true' and 'let every man be a liar', are one group. The optative 'may it not be' is an exclamation, not a command, and 'part' is not an imperative member role.
The quoted psalm as a unit: the citation formula is its frame and the quoted words are its parts. No writer is named, so there is no sender.

none_fit.where: cl2 'every man a liar, just as it is written'
none_fit.what: Scripture cited as backing for the claim just before it. The 'as' type's fulfilment sense applies only to an earlier word, so no link type fits fully.
A rejection of the claim in 3:3; no link type records a disavowal of the preceding question.

none_fit.where: cl5 to cl6 (ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαι, 'when being judged')
none_fit.what: A temporal 'when' clause has no link type of its own; recorded as within, with the temporal role stated in why.

none_fit.where: 3:4 cl0 and cl1 ('Certainly not!' then 'let God be true')
none_fit.what: A denial followed by a counter-jussive, joined by de; no link type records a rebuttal.

cant_tell.what: the purpose reading of cl1 to cl4
cant_tell.why: Whether the quoted ὅπως clause states God's aim in being true, or only the psalm's own purpose, is a reading; I added the link because the form allows it, and it is open to review.
